stops.note: 'bell', probably imitative; Irish monks such as St Columbanus carried hand-bells on their missions across Europe around 600
the Irish word entered the Latin of the Church, giving French cloche and German Glocke 'bell'
'bell', and by extension a timepiece that struck the hours on a bell
the first mechanical clocks told time only by striking bells; Salisbury Cathedral's clock of about 1386 is often called the oldest working clock in the world

current_meaning: an instrument for measuring and showing the time
